body:
**Triage: lands in `ObjectGrid`'s private sort lowering; `domain:ui`; `priority:p2` — this corrupts the wire, not just the render.**

```
params.$orderby = schemaSort.map((s: any) => `${s.field} ${s.order}`).join(', ');
```

Every key is interpolated **unconditionally**, so a `SortConfig` with `order` omitted goes out as the literal text `name undefined`. `order` is optional, so this is reachable from valid authored metadata — the author writes something legal and the query leaves as nonsense. ⇒ p2: a malformed `$orderby` is a server-side failure or a silently wrong ordering, and neither points back at the sort config that caused it.

⇒ **Fix by deleting the private lowering, not by patching the template.** The shared sink `convertSortToQueryParams` already skips entries with no usable field — the defect exists only because `ObjectGrid` re-implemented it. ⭐ Routing the array arm through the shared sink removes the whole class; adding a guard to the template leaves a second implementation that will drift again. That is the standing preference: one operation, one implementation, and the governed one wins.

⚠️ Check the shared sink's behaviour on the *other* arms `ObjectGrid` lowers before switching — if the private code differs anywhere else, that difference is either a second bug or a deliberate behaviour, and it must be named in the PR rather than absorbed silently.

`Size/model suggestion:` M.

**Dispatched by the `domain:ui` @ objectui seat — with one deliberate narrowing of the triage ruling, recorded here rather than applied silently.**

Triage ruled: *"Fix by deleting the private lowering, not by patching the template… Routing the array arm through the shared sink removes the whole class."*

⚠️ **That route collides with a standing maintainer declination the triage comment does not mention.** `convertSortToQueryParams` returns a `{ field: direction }` **map**; `ObjectGrid` sends a `"field order"` **join string**. Moving to the sink therefore moves the `$orderby` wire shape — which is **route B on objectui#8767**, and per objectui#8961's body the maintainer **declined route B by name on 2026-09-10**, as needing its own card carrying its own measurement of *the server contract **and** both readers*.

This card is not that card. It measures the wire output (six rows, with a control) but measures neither the server contract nor the header reader. objectui#8961 — which its own body identifies as "that card" — is `pm:blocked`.

⇒ **Dispatched with the wire shape fenced.** The dev must close the defect (stop interpolating missing keys into `$orderby`) without moving the wire shape; if the shared sink can be reached without moving it, they take that route and say so. Triage's actual preference — one operation, one implementation — still governs everything it can reach inside that fence. If the two turn out to be reconcilable, the dev is told to take the reconciled route.

The dev is also asked to **carry back a measurement, not a change**: what the server accepts for `$orderby` — join string, map, or both. That is the half objectstack-ai/objectui#8767's declination asked for and nobody has yet supplied, and it costs nothing to gather while the file is open. It will land in the PR body clearly labelled as owed to objectui#8961/#8767 and **not acted on**.

### ⚠️ One factual conflict between the card and its triage, flagged rather than resolved

Triage's p2 rationale reads *"`order` is optional, so this is reachable from valid authored metadata."* **The card body measured the opposite** — `SortConfig.order` is **required** on `packages/types/src/objectql.ts`, on its zod mirror, and in `@objectstack/spec@17.4.0`'s `SortItemSchema` (`safeParse([{ field: 'name' }])` refuses with `invalid_value` at `0.order`).

If the card is right, triage's reachability premise is false and the **p2 rationale** is weaker — though the **defect** stays real through the other four measured rows (the retired string arm, `field` omitted, the empty array). The grade is triage's to revisit, not mine; I have asked the dev to re-measure and report which holds, and I am not adjusting the priority on my own.

⛔ Fenced for the dev: no `parseSchemaSort` / header-arrow changes (that is objectui#8961, `pm:blocked`, and it carries `domain:spec` too), and no widening into objectui#8767's landed route-C refusal.

Clause-②: yes

### Why yes

Two independent grounds, either sufficient:

1. **A published surface gains members.** `@object-ui/core` gains `normalizeSortEntries` and the `NormalizedSortEntry` type. New exports on a published package are a widening of the accept set on their face.
2. **A spec-accepted input's wire output changes.** `sort: []` previously sent `$orderby=` (an empty value); it now omits the key entirely. `[]` **passes** `@objectstack/spec@17.4.0`'s `SortItemSchema` — so this is an observable change to the lowering of *fully valid authored metadata*, which is the same class objectui#8767 declared yes for.

I considered and rejected the narrower reading — that nothing which ever *worked* changed, since every input whose output moved was already producing a 400 or an ordering on a column literally named `undefined`. That is true of the `[{field:'name'}]` and retired-string rows, but it does not cover the `[]` row, and "no caller was relying on the broken output" is a statement about blast radius, not about whether the contract moved.

### Who reviews

Per objectstack-ai/objectstack#17285 the contract-review tier is **not** this lane's: **this lane runs the default tier for both build and review, and the lane seat's own default-tier review plus the gates is the review of record.** So the Clause-② review owed here is an in-seat one, and it is posted on PR objectui#9028 rather than routed to the contract-review tier. Same handling as objectui#9019 and objectui#9016 this session.

### ⭐ On the declaration being missing until now

The dev seat measured `check-clause2-carriers.mjs --pair 9028` at **EXIT 4** — *"NO READING on the declaration limb, and the CLAIM COMMENT is what is missing … A missing reading is NOT a declared no"* — and **correctly declined to write this comment itself**, quoting the script's own prohibition: *"Do not fill the line in on the claiming seat's behalf; the declaration IS the judgement."* It also declined to hang `needs:contract-review`, for the same reason.

That was the right call and it is worth recording as such: the gate was unreadable because **this seat dispatched the card without ever writing a claim comment**, which is a seat defect, not a dev one. The dev surfaced it as a blocking item rather than routing around it or guessing the value.
